Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36594: net: make orphan reconsideration more granular

83003cafaa81bb116526419246608658ede824b6 qa: test a single orphan is processed per peer turn, regardless of its validation result (Antoine Poinsot)
28a41e61ab5d993d344dc5c8180482eb146c6bd5 net: reconsider at most one orphan per call, whatever the validation result (Antoine Poinsot)

Pull request description:

  We currently concentrate the validation of all the assigned peer’s reconsiderable orphans that are still missing inputs in a single message-processing turn. This ties orphan processing to validation result, and adds latency to processing other peers' messages.

  Always process a single reconsiderable orphan per turn instead. This removes the need for an immediate validation result, and shifts the latency from other peers to the assigned peer.

  #35829 made the fields of `HTTPRequest` & `HTTPRemoteClient` private, but still allows anyone with a reference to a request to update the internal state `enum`. https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35829#discussion_r3860447518

  `HTTPRemoteClient::TryReadRequest()` only needs to be a `static` method in order to forward a `shared_ptr` of a client to a new request.

  ### Commits solving these issues in same order

  * http: Remove `HTTPRequest::SetState()` and introduce `HTTPRequest::Load()` - Removes the ability for other classes to directly modify the request state.
  * 2 refactors: Extract `HTTPRemoteClient::TryReadRequestInternal()` from a combination of `HTTPRemoteClient::TryReadRequest()` and `HTTPRemoteClient::ReadRequest()` (the latter is removed)

Pull request description:

  Convert `remove` and `remove_if` to the C++20 `std::erase` and `std::erase_if` overloads.

  The legacy ones can be confusing, because:

  * Array-based containers (like vector) must use the erase-remove idiom.   * They are more verbose.

  Also convert simple iterator-erase (which is verbose, but fine) to the std overload.

12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056 validation: return block-file flush errors (Lőrinc)
07d23eb75527b8dd6571a33b3bc304815764bc07 test: characterize writes after flush failure (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** When flushing block or undo data fails, `FlushStateToDisk()` still writes block-index metadata and coins data, then advances `m_last_flushed_block`.
  With a separate `-blocksdir`, persistent failures there can leave metadata referring to block data that is not durable even when chainstate writes succeed.

  **Fix:** Return the flush error before those writes, leaving the last-flushed marker and on-disk coins tip unchanged in the failing call.
  Later flushes can retry and write if they succeed, including during shutdown.
  `ConnectTip()` and `DisconnectTip()` propagate the error before updating the chain tip, after applying the coins changes in memory.

  **History:**
  * [#27866](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/27866#discussion_r1297313148) raised whether saving other state after a flush failure was preferable. This change preserves later retries while skipping writes in the failing call.
  * [#34897](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34897) introduced `m_last_flushed_block` to prevent persistent indexes from advancing past flushed chainstate. This fix keeps it at the last successful flush.

commit.message:
cli: fail to send a request when the socket does not become writable

HTTPClient::SendRequest() waits for the socket to become writable and
went back to waiting whenever Sock::Wait() returned without SendEvent.
Before 1805716354, the `continue` was the route to the deadline check. That
commit removed the deadline, so a Sock::Wait() timeout silently started
waiting again, forever. This means -rpcclienttimeout is never respected
when sending: bitcoin-cli will hang for as long as the server keeps the
connection open without reading the request.

Fix this by returning a failure whenever `Sock::Wait()` timeouts or errors.

cf30d0a4123bb4237495f04e723ce9f706c2edf2 subprocess: fix command line memory leak on Windows (stickies-v)

Pull request description:

  `Popen::execute_process()` copied the command line into a buffer from `new[]`, but did not delete it. This leaked memory each time a process started on Windows.

  `CreateProcessA` [needs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessa#:~:text=characters%2E-,The,violation) a writable command line buffer. Since C++17, `std::string::data()` supplies one, so give the `std::string` buffer directly and remove the copy.

  This only affects Windows. It is only reachable if `-signer=<cmd>` is set, through authenticated RPC or the GUI. Each call leaks only the startup-defined `<cmd>`, and the rate is limited by process spawn time, so the impact is limited.

  _edit: this was fixed upstream in https://github.com/arun11299/cpp-subprocess/pull/131, but since this codebase is C++20 it seems better to avoid the copy (and the const cast). A direct backport isn't possible anyway, since #35704 switched us to CreateProcessA._

commit.message:
net: reconsider at most one orphan per call, whatever the validation result

Orphan processing used to be uninterruptible, which could be exploited
as a severe CPU DoS (see CVE-2024-52914). 866c8058a7 mitigated this by
interrupting orphan processing after the first transaction validation
that did not result in a missing input error.

This commit moves the interruption point to after each transaction
validation, whatever the result. This unties it from the validation
result and reduces the latency before processing other peers' messages,
at the cost of increasing it for the messages of the peer the orphans
are assigned to.

5a4cd70547096af6247167d8dde6145a1b548642 Test: Add P2SH scriptSig stack-size boundary tests (benthecarman)

Pull request description:

  VerifyScript runs a P2SH scriptPubKey on the stack the scriptSig leaves before handling the redeemScript. The 20-byte push in HASH160 <20> EQUAL adds one item, so a scriptSig that leaves 1,000 items fails with STACK_SIZE, while 999 items is valid.

  An implementation that checks the redeemScript hash without running the scriptPubKey accepts the 1,000-item spend. No existing vector leaves the scriptSig at this boundary, so such an implementation can pass every row.

  Add 999 and 1,000 item cases with P2SH and WITNESS, and the 1,000 item case with no flags, which fails the same way because the scriptPubKey always runs. 5aaaf7b8d1ed72b7ab9eee117204f4c4346eb235 test: check network filtering and uniformity of addrman Select (Pieter Wuille)
9a0e095c687d7e139a9571883296cd9321e5beeb addrman: use uniform sampling inside buckets (Pieter Wuille)

Pull request description:

  The current way we sample from addresses within a bucket in addrman is randomized, but not perfectly random. It uses a linear scan, starting at a random position (out of the 64 positions in a bucket). This means that if for example only position 17 and 20 contain an address, 17 will be picked with probability 95.3% (whenever the initial position is 21..63 or 0..17) and 20 will be picked with probability 4.7% (whenever the initial position is 18..20).

  Make this search perfectly uniform, regardless of distribution of addresses within the bucket, by first copying all non-empty positions to a temporary array, and then selecting uniformly randomly from that array.

  Suggested by Crypt-iQ. Also pointed out earlier by mzumsande in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/23140#discussion_r733084509.

Unreachable error also honors `G_ABORT_ON_FAILED_ASSUME`, and if set,
it aborts instead of throwing.
The condition checking `G_ABORT_ON_FAILED_ASSUME` has been extracted
into a new helper, `internal_non_fatal_helper()`, and it is reused.
